summary: Norway's Equinor says it is dealing with an ongoing cyberattack on some IT systems. It says oil and gas output is not affected. The NSA outage is blamed on maintenance, and no official source links the recent outages. US stocks fell again on Nov 17, but futures are up today.

events.title: Norway's Equinor reports an ongoing cyberattack on some IT systems
events.impact: Equinor says production and operations are not affected and it sees no sign of stolen data. Norway's security authority NSM says it is in contact with the company.
events.stated_cause: Equinor calls it a cyberattack. Who did it and how they got in are unknown.

events.title: NSA classified internal network (NSANet) disrupted
events.impact: CNN says the campus went to essential staff only while the network is restored, and the fix was not complete. NSA says mission-critical work continued.
events.stated_cause: NSA says routine maintenance. The Director of National Intelligence says a software patch for flaws found last month. No official source reports a cyber attack.

events.title: FAA nationwide ground stop; router installs paused
events.impact: About 12,462 flights were cancelled on Nov 13. The FAA paused Juniper router installs and turned off one function on more than 60 similar routers. A House hearing is set for today.
events.stated_cause: FAA says a new router sent out a flood of data that overloaded old equipment. HPE says its gear worked as configured. Root cause is not yet known. FAA reports no sign of a cyberattack.

events.title: S&P 500 fell a fourth day; futures up after Nvidia
events.impact: On Nov 17 the S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 and the Dow fell 1.64%. S&P futures are up about 0.4% today. I saw no trading halts or exchange glitches.
events.stated_cause: Reports cite worry about AI stock values, rates and Nvidia's leadership change. One report says the NSA outage news added to selling.

events.title: Bitcoin near 64-65K USD, down about 12-13% on the week
events.impact: Price data shows BTC near 64K-65K, roughly flat to slightly lower over 24 hours. This is a gradual slide, not a crash. I found no exchange outage.
events.stated_cause: Price sites give no cause. One market note says traders expect a possible Fed rate hike next month.

events.title: Apple services (iCloud, Apple Pay, App Store) outage
events.impact: Thousands of outage-tracker reports. Apple said many systems were back up afterward.
events.stated_cause: Apple says an internal update caused it. Apple told Bloomberg it was not a cyberattack.

events.title: Chase banking services disrupted
events.impact: Some Chase customers could not use certain services on Monday. Chase now looks operational.
events.stated_cause: Chase says a software bug in an on-premise hardware system caused it, and it is not cyber-related.

events.title: Marriott sign-in outage on website and Bonvoy app
events.impact: Some guests could not sign in or check in for a time. Marriott says it is fixed.
events.stated_cause: Marriott says a technical issue. Its review found no sign of a cyberattack.

events.title: United Airlines tech outage delays departures
events.impact: Some United departures were delayed on Monday. United said it was resolved.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. United called it a technology issue. No official source links it to the FAA event.

events.title: Hackers reportedly planted malicious code on sites of up to 178 organizations
events.impact: Newsweek says visitors' personal and financial data could be exposed. A live blog also mentions a security incident at a digital tools platform used by big firms. I could not confirm details.
events.stated_cause: Described as hackers planting code. Who did it and how are unknown.

events.title: AT&T and Spectrum user complaints on outage trackers
events.impact: Hundreds of user reports for AT&T and mixed data for Spectrum. No carrier confirmation or wire report seen. Looks like normal background noise.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. No carrier has given a cause.

events.title: Routine CISA notices on actively exploited flaws
events.impact: CISA keeps adding exploited bugs to its known-exploited list and posting routine advisories. I saw no new Emergency Directive in the last 3 days.
events.stated_cause: Attackers exploiting software flaws. No notice links to the outages above.

connection_assessment.reasoning: FAA: a new router flooded old gear with data; root cause unknown. NSA: maintenance patch. Apple: internal update. Chase: software bug. Equinor: cyberattack, culprit unknown. No official source links any of them; Rubio said he has zero information of a link.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official statement blaming the same company or attacker, or Equinor's attacker being tied to the US outages, would make me think they are connected.

alert.reason: Equinor's attack is confirmed but says it has not hit production, and nothing officially links it to the US outages.

prep_note: No action needed for most people. Keep some cash on hand and use your usual bank app, in case of short outages. Allow extra time for flights and check airline apps before leaving. Be careful with unexpected emails or login pages. Businesses that use Juniper routers or Equinor systems should watch vendor notices.
